intent.raw: Run a small dual-lane dialectic to determine whether the proposed RWO canonical identity contract needs refinement.
intent.objective: Produce verified KEEP/FIX requests for RWO-JCS-SAFEINT-V1 from independent formal-interoperability and adversarial domain-lifecycle concerns before owner acceptance.

steps.name: Run and confront two canonical-contract attack lanes
convergence_criteria: both lanes return final positions after one bounded confrontation
every MAJOR finding has current evidence and a discriminating counterexample
the parent can classify each proposed refinement as retained, refuted, or unresolved without selecting the owner gate
stop_conditions: stop if a lane edits the target or exceeds the named source corpus
stop if a finding lacks current file evidence or an official primary-standard selector
stop if the lanes remain irreconcilable after one confrontation
stop on any implementation, ontology, authority, promotion, publication, deployment, or release mutation

gates.condition: No review role may spawn and no ledger row may append until the user confirms the validated, double-PASS material strategy.
Both reviewers are joined and closed with evidenced final positions and discriminating counterexamples before parent synthesis.
Review evidence cannot select the contract option, mutate target artifacts, unblock Invoke, or claim implementation, authority, promotion, publication, deployment, release, or production readiness.

boundaries.contract: Current contract, language-refinement, and way-maker bytes are immutable review inputs; reviewers return evidence only.
Each lane returns a structured lifecycle receipt and final evidenced position; prose without required evidence cannot open synthesis.
No review role may spawn until the human confirms the materially frozen strategy.

authority.validation: dispatch-spec, register-dispatch readiness, two independent tension verdicts, parent source verification
authority.evidence: review findings owned by the parent as non-authority decision input
authority.memory: Inventory is a non-authority discovery projection

subagent_strategy.trigger: Two independent concerns can attack the same existing contract in parallel, and their disagreement should be preserved before owner acceptance.
subagent_strategy.explanation: One formal lane attacks cross-language byte reproducibility; one adversarial lane attacks semantic and lifecycle sufficiency. Their bounded confrontation prevents either deterministic serialization or architectural boundary concerns from dominating by default.
context: The RWO contract is a pending Decision Gate artifact, not an accepted owner decision.
The current Work Pack remains unchanged and implementation has not started.
Review outputs are private non-authority evidence only.
subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Reply confirmed to authorize registration and the exact two-agent read-only dialectic.

roles.purpose: Prove or refute unambiguous canonical bytes and fixtures across Python, Rust, and Go.
Attack semantic sufficiency, evolution, fixture governance, and transport/runtime ownership leakage.

agents.residue: No executed Python/Rust/Go vectors; target Inventory source coverage blocked.
agents.reroute: human decision gate over the verified change-request list

agents.residue: Target Inventory source coverage blocked; schema/reducer migration owner unresolved; no executed cross-language conformance.

validation: Formal corpus and primary-standard review passed; confrontation converged.
native_stage_receipts.handoff_note: Parent synthesis may consume the verified formal change requests.

validation: Domain/lifecycle corpus review passed; every MAJOR finding has a discriminating scenario; confrontation converged.
native_stage_receipts.residue: Target Inventory coverage remains blocked and no cross-language vectors were executed.
native_stage_receipts.handoff_note: Parent synthesis may consume the verified domain/lifecycle change requests.

promotion_guardrails: The review cannot choose or accept the Decision Gate option.
Inventory and adjacent strategies are discovery context, not proof.
No review output may mutate the RWO contract, Work Pack, implementation, ontology, authority, publication, deployment, or release state.
Protobuf/gRPC, journal, retry, ARE, and runtime surfaces remain consumers or separate owners, not canonical kernel identity.
